message.content: /deep-research Which of the UK-born individuals who won The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences while being affiliated with a UK based institution, between the inception of the award and the year that the first woman won The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, has fewer than 20 "Articles" listed on ideas.repec.org that have a publication year prior to the year that they won the award?

tasks.goal: Create a research plan for identifying UK-born Nobel Economics laureates (1969-2009) affiliated with UK institutions at time of award, then checking their RePEc article counts pre-award
tasks.context: Need to: 1) List all Nobel Economics laureates 1969-2009, 2) Filter for UK-born + UK-affiliated at award time, 3) For each, check ideas.repec.org for 'Articles' count with publication year < award year, 4) Identify those with <20 such articles. First woman winner was Elinor Ostrom in 2009.

Need complete list of Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences laureates from 1969 (first award) through 2009 (Elinor Ostrom - first woman winner). For each: name, year, birth country, institutional affiliation at time of award. Official Nobel site and reliable secondary sources.
tasks.goal: Find all Nobel Economics laureates 1969-2009 with birth country and institutional affiliation at award time

tasks.context: First query results will provide the full laureate list. Need to identify which were born in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland). Verify birth countries from authoritative sources.
tasks.goal: Filter the 1969-2009 laureates for those born in the United Kingdom

tasks.context: From the UK-born laureates, need to verify which were affiliated with a UK-based institution at the exact time of their Nobel award. Check official Nobel citations and institutional histories.
tasks.goal: Identify which UK-born laureates had UK institutional affiliation at award time

input.query: Nobel Memorial Prize Economic Sciences laureates 1969 2009 list birth country affiliation

# All prizes in economic sciences

The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel has been awarded 57 times to 99 laureates between 1969 and 2025. Click on the links to get more information.

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2025](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2025/summary/)

> “for having explained innovation-driven economic growth”

[Joel Mokyr](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2025/mokyr/facts/)

> “for having identified the prerequisites for sustained growth through technological progress”

[Philippe Aghion](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2025/aghion/facts/) and [Peter Howitt](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2025/howitt/facts/)

> “for the theory of sustained growth through creative destruction”

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2024](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/summary/)

[Daron Acemoglu](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/acemoglu/facts/), [Simon Johnson](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/johnson/facts/) and [James A. Robinson](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/robinson/facts/)

> “for studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity”

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2023](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2023/summary/)

[Claudia Goldin](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2023/goldin/facts/)

> “for having advanced our understanding of women’s labour market outcomes”

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2022](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2022/summary/)

[Ben Bernanke](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2022/bernanke/facts/), [Douglas Diamond](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2022/diamond/facts/) and [Philip Dybvig](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2022/dybvig/facts/)

> “for research on banks and financial crises”

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2021](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2021/summary/)

[David Card](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2021/card/facts/)

> “for his empirical contributions to labour economics”

[Joshua D. Angrist](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2021/angrist/facts/) and [Guido W. Imbens](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2021/imbens/facts/)

> “for their methodological contributions to the analysis of causal relationships”

### [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2020](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2020/summary/)

[Paul R. Milgrom](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2020/milgrom/facts/) and [Robert B. Wilson](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2020/wilson/facts/)

> “for improvements to auction theory and inventions of new auction formats”

118|The announcement of the 2008 [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") in Nobel Prize Press Conference. The laureate of the Prize was [Paul Krugman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Krugman "Paul Krugman").
119|
120|The **Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences**, officially the **Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel")**[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) ([Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Sveriges riksbanks pris i ekonomisk vetenskap till Alfred Nobels minne*), commonly referred to as the **Nobel Prize in Economics**, is an award in the field of [Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Sciences "Economic Sciences") administered by the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation").[[4]](#cite_note-NobelPrizeSelectionProcess-4)
121|
122|The first Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded in 1969 to [Ragnar Frisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragnar_Frisch "Ragnar Frisch") and [Jan Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Tinbergen "Jan Tinbergen").[[5]](#cite_note-Winners1969-5) Each recipient receives a [medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal "Medal"), a [diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma "Diploma") and a monetary award that has varied throughout the years.[[6]](#cite_note-NobelPrizeDescription-6) In 1969, Frisch and Tinbergen were given a combined 375,000 [SEK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), which is equivalent to 2,871,041 SEK in December 2007. The award is presented in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") at an annual ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[7]](#cite_note-7)
123|
124|As of the awarding of the 2023 prize, 55 Prizes in Economic Sciences have been given to 93 individuals.[[8]](#cite_note-NobelLaureatesList-8) As of October 2023, the department of economics with the most affiliated [laureates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureate "Laureate") in economic sciences is the [University of Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago "University of Chicago"),[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10) with 16 affiliated laureates. As of 2023, the institutions with the most [PhD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") (or equivalent) graduates who went on to receive the prize are Harvard University and MIT (13 each), followed by the University of Chicago (10). As of 2024, the institutions with the most affiliated faculty at the time of the award are the University of Chicago (15), followed by MIT (10), then by Princeton University and Harvard University (8 each).

## Abstract

Ronald Coase wrote two great theoretical articles that earned him the Nobel Prize: "The Nature of the Firm" in 1937 and "The Problem of Social Cost" in 1960. He also wrote many articles dealing with the methodology of economics, often in the setting of a discussion of a particular economist, such as Adam Smith or Alfred Marshall. The methodological articles will be my particular focus here.

## Summary

**UK-born, UK-affiliated Nobel Economics laureates (1969–2009):**
| Laureate | Award Year | Birth Country | Affiliation at Award | Pre-award RePEc Articles |
|----------|------------|---------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| John Hicks | 1972 | England | University of Oxford | ~30 |
| James Meade | 1977 | England | University of Cambridge | 20 |
| **Richard Stone** | **1984** | **England** | **University of Cambridge** | **18** |
| Ronald Coase | 1991 | England | LSE / U. Chicago | 26 |
| James Mirrlees | 1996 | Scotland | University of Cambridge | 25 |
| Clive Granger | 2003 | Wales | UC San Diego (US) | — (not UK-affiliated) |

**Richard Stone** is the only one with **fewer than 20 "Articles" on IDEAS/RePEc published strictly before his award year (1984)**. His profile shows 18 journal articles with publication years 1938–1982 (items 11–28 in the Articles list). The 1984 publications (items 8–10) are not counted since the criterion is "publication year prior to the year that they won the award."
